No dip-buying: Thursday also saw a notable change in trader behavior. Retail investors abandoned their signature dip-buying playbook to dump individual stocks at the fastest pace since March 2020. Shortly before market close, retail net outflows from single stocks reached $338M, Vanda Research noted. The selloff marked the third-largest day of retail single-stock liquidation on record, trailing only March 12 and March 17 of 2020. Vanda analyst Viraj Patel said institutional call buying slumped to a one-year low earlier in the week, while leveraged ETFs faced an estimated $42B-$48B in forced rebalancing into the close alongside de-risking from volatility-target funds. With institutional buyers stepping aside just as retail and systematic strategies aggressively unload equities, Patel warned that the collision represents flow dynamics rarely witnessed outside periods of acute market stress.

A imprensa de esquerda bem pode muito fabricar os titulos que quer, mas como a geringonça provou nao é quem tem mais votos, é quem consegue formar governo.
Actualmente ha uma maioria clara de portugueses a votar no PSD e no Chega. Mesmo que o PS tenha mais que qualquer um dos outros dois…quem está a ver o PSD ou o Chega a empossar um governo PS?

Mas confesso que gostaria de ver o PS e o resto da esquerda a argumentar que deveriam deixar o “partido mais votado governar” depois do que fizeram em 2015
